source_record.english: Sutra also mentions the "eight expressions of a realized person"--four where you say "I did see it" about things you really did see and so on; four where you say "I didn't see it" about things you really didn't see and such. Regarding these two sets of eight, one may ask for a more detailed description of the basic four: what it is to be "something seen," "something heard," and so on. That which is experienced by consciousness of the eye, consciousness of the ear, consciousness of the thought, and by the other three kinds of consciousness (those of nose, tongue, and body) represents respectively what is seen, what is heard, what is known, and also what is sensed. We turn next to a description of the six "branch" non-virtues. 78 Six "Branch" Non-Virtues
